memory_update.text: AXTI should be retained as the highest-priority underfollowed U.S.-listed direct substrate candidate for the optical_interconnect_substrates node; verify InP backlog conversion, export permits, customer qualification, and capacity expansion.
VECO should be retained as an upstream equipment bottleneck candidate tied to InP laser and 800G/1.6T optical-component capacity expansion.
ALMU is a speculative shadow candidate only; do not promote beyond Layer 1 unless named customer qualification, production yield, and commercial AI-photonics revenue evidence appear.

For this node, the practical chokepoint may split into at least three layers: native InP substrate supply, InP laser/photonic-device manufacturing tools, and downstream 800G/1.6T module qualification.

Need a primary-source map of which U.S.-listed companies have direct 800G/1.6T customer qualification versus merely broad photonics exposure; current evidence is strongest for AXTI, VECO, and COHR, weaker for ALMU.

node: Precision optical substrates and materials for 800G/1.6T transceivers
summary: Layer 1B expands the U.S.-listed universe around the upstream optical-materials chokepoint for AI data-center interconnects. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is AXTI, an InP/GaAs/Ge substrate supplier with explicit data-center InP revenue and backlog evidence. VECO maps to the equipment bottleneck for scaling InP laser production. ALMU is a speculative shadow candidate attempting an alternative InP-on-silicon/III-V-on-silicon scaling route. COHR is included as a high-attention reference anchor because it commercializes 800G/1.6T transceiver and InP-enabled photonics products downstream of the substrate/tooling layer.
